overview: I'm grateful that President Trump and Secretary McMahon are committed to reforming our broken education system so that it works better for American students and their families. We lack direct evidence of a causal link between smartphones and learning, but I'm convinced that this technology is a key driver of youth mental health challenges, a distraction from learning both inside and outside of schools, and a deterrent to reading when NAPE surveys reveal that many fewer students read on their own for fun. As we speak, the president and the secretary of the department, Secretary McMahon, have delayed billions of dollars of funding and canceled critical grant programs. So in the midst of all of this chaos that we are seeing at the Department of Education, I am really concerned about the latest results of the National Report Card which came out this month because it does show that while Trump is pushing ahead with tearing apart the Department of Education and ripping resources away from our students, our kids are continuing to fall behind. Trump cut $1 billion in funding for mental health care in schools, including a program in Massachusetts training 50 school psychologists to work in high-need districts. So for months, Trump administration illegally withheld $7 billion in funding, including $108 million from Massachusetts that supports English learners after school programs and more throwing school and town budgets across Massachusetts and the country into chaos.
context: **Committee**: Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions
